newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Zim Israel Navigation seeks strategic partner.
newsitem.headline: Zim Israel Navigation seeks strategic partner.

text.p: Israel Corp is holding talks with several potential strategic partners for its subsidiary Zim Israel Navigation Co, an Israel Corp spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Talks are currently underway with several major companies," the spokesman said.
Israel Corp holds nearly 50 percent of Zim, Israel's biggest shipping company and one of the world's 10 largest. The remaining shares are controlled by the Israeli government.

The spokesman said the decision to seek out a strategic partner was done with the approval of the government following repeated failures to take Zim public. Zim has tried on three separate occasions over the last few years to float shares.

Zim reported net profit of $14.8 million on revenues of $1.43 billion in 1995. In the first half of 1996, net income rose 20 percent to $4.2 million on a slight decline in revenues. Although Zim was profitable, the world shipping industry is in crisis, which has prompted a number of mergers.
Israel Corp is a holding company controlled by industrialist Shoul Eisenberg, a leading international businessman based in Israel.
